_readme: Example only. Copy nothing from this file by hand: run node init-family.mjs --name <your-name> --adults <n> --children <n> --days <n> and it writes profiles/family-<your-name>.json from YOUR orders. Every key here is a key the planner reads, so you know what to look for. The _note lines say which numbers the miners measure and which are yours to change.
name: family-example

household._note: timezone is where the planner counts days; who eats and how much is under dinners.members.

dinners._members_note: appetite 1.0 is an adult, 0.6 a small child, 1.2 a teenager; the planner sums count x appetite for the portions a night.
dinners.servingsPerDinner: derived: members x appetite x nights

budget.softCapKr: median order x orders per period

learning._note: learn.mjs compares each plan with the basket that followed it. Nothing here is edited by it; it writes profiles/learned.json, which your profile always outranks.

basket.existingQuantityRule: max(existing, planned) except for a line that came with a recipe card, which the plan overwrites
basket._note: The same basket is shared with the phone app, so nothing is ever deleted automatically.

purchasing._note: How a pack is chosen. The planner covers the need for the lowest TOTAL price, never for the best price per unit. A food that keeps may overrun the need by a lot, because the price rule already stops it from costing more; fresh food may only overrun it by overshootPctFresh.
purchasing._stableWords_note: Words in a product name that mean extra of it is not waste. Eggs keep for weeks, so 15 bought for a need of 12 is a saving; 400 g of salmon for 300 g needed is waste. Matching is by substring, so freshWords are checked FIRST and always win: 'salt' would otherwise read inside 'saltet' and call butter a keepsake. Anything neither list names is treated as fresh.
purchasing._maxOverrunFreshMl_note: A little extra of a fresh thing is not waste: 40 g of curry powder for a need of 50 g is cheaper than the smaller pack, 400 g of extra salmon is not. Grams and millilitres both count.

rule.always: compare price per kg (Namlig UnitPriceCalc), not the pack price
rule.fat: lean mince: 8-12% for beef and pork, 7-10% for poultry; never buy the 19-23% mince
rule.quality: no organic premium unless it is within 10% of the conventional price per kg
rule.cut: the cut we buy is the cheap one per kg: chicken breast instead of tenderloin, dark fish fillet instead of salmon, unless salmon is on sale
rule.child: no whole bones in a dinner for a small child: mince, fillet or strips only

perProtein._note: buy / fatBands / maxKrPerKg / never, per protein, from your cart

meat.priceRule: always compare price per kg, never the pack price

exclusions.freshHerbs: never buy the fresh herbs a recipe asks for
